newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-HUBER LOSES IN FIRST SHOCK OF ITALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HUBER LOSES IN FIRST SHOCK OF ITALIAN OPEN.

text.p: Teenage wild card Francesca Lubiani caused the first shock of the Italian Open women's tennis tournament on Wednesday with a second round defeat of fourth-seeded German Anke Huber.

The 19-year-old Italian, ranked 73rd in the world, beat her eighth-ranked opponent 6-2 6-4 in a match that could have been even more humiliating but for a late rally by the German, who was subsequently reported to be feeling unwell.

Huber, the second seed to fall at the Foro Italico after 15th seeded Frenchwoman Nathalie Tauziat on Tuesday, was 5-1 down in the second set with Lubiani to serve but pulled herself back from the brink with a crucial break.
The Italian twice took the score to deuce, saving two break points, but could not provide the killer shots.

Huber then held her serve to narrow to 5-3 and Lubiani, after saving three break points without once having a match point herself, then hit a return to the net to allow her opponent to break back into the match at 5-4.
But then the German ran out of steam.
Huber's already erratic serve deserted her and, with Lubiani enjoying two match points, saved her opponent the bother of providing a winning shot by double-faulting into the net.
An official said Huber, who did not attend a post match news conference, was unwell and seeing a doctor.
She said the Women's Tennis Association (WTA) would release a statement later.
Lubiani now meets either Adriana Gersi of the Czech Republic or Austrian 11th seed Barbara Paulus.
"Its the most important win of my career," said the Bolognese winner, who is coached by her father.
"I knew she was the most erratic of the top 10, the most beatable, I knew I could win."

Few Italians had been so confident and, with the match played at a time when many of her compatriots were still enjoying their lunches, her heroics were played out before fans outnumbered by empty seats around the centre court.
Two other seeds went through to the round of 16, with Romanian Ruxandra Dragomir avoiding Huber's fate after also losing the first set against Belgian Els Callens.
Dragomir won 3-6 6-2 6-0 and now faces either second seed Iva Majoli of Croatia or American Nicole Arendt.
Russian 12th seed Elena Likhovtseva had a far easier time beating Latvian Larisa Neiland 6-3 6-3.
